title: Synonyms and Meaning
text:
Good writers rarely repeat the same word again and again. Instead, they replace it with a synonym that carries a similar meaning. However, true synonyms are rare, because almost every pair of words differs slightly in connotation. A writer must therefore choose a replacement that fits both the meaning and the tone of the sentence. A mismatch can make a text sound awkward or even change its message.

Translators face the same problem when moving a text between languages. A word that seems equivalent may carry cultural associations that the target readers do not share. Consequently, many translators prefer to restate an idea completely rather than replace each word. This approach preserves the intended effect, even when the sentence structure looks very different.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, why are true synonyms rare?
options: Almost every pair of words differs slightly in connotation
They are only found in dictionaries
They always change the length of a sentence

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do many translators prefer to do?
What can be inferred about a word that seems equivalent in another language?
options: It always has the same connotations
It may carry associations that foreign readers do not share
It is never useful for translation
It is only used in spoken language

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the second paragraph?
options: To show why restating an idea can be safer than word-for-word replacement
To explain how dictionaries are written
To argue that synonyms should be avoided

vocabulary.definition: a word with a similar meaning to another word
an additional idea or feeling a word suggests
having the same value or meaning

paragraph_translations: Bons escritores raramente repetem a mesma palavra várias vezes. Em vez disso, substituem-na por um sinônimo com significado semelhante. No entanto, sinônimos verdadeiros são raros, pois quase todo par de palavras difere levemente em conotação. Um escritor deve, portanto, escolher um substituto que se encaixe tanto no sentido quanto no tom da frase. Uma incompatibilidade pode deixar o texto estranho ou até mudar sua mensagem.

Tradutores enfrentam o mesmo problema ao transferir um texto entre idiomas. Uma palavra que parece equivalente pode carregar associações culturais que os leitores da língua de destino não compartilham. Consequentemente, muitos tradutores preferem reformular a ideia por completo em vez de substituir cada palavra. Essa abordagem preserva o efeito pretendido, mesmo quando a estrutura da frase parece muito diferente.
